newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-CRICKET- Germon demands tough mental attitude.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-CRICKET- Germon demands tough mental attitude.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Jan 22 - New Zealand must take a tough mental attitude into their three-test cricket series against England, according to captain Lee Germon.
The Bank of New Zealand Series starts at Eden Park on Friday and there's no question England will go in with the better preparation.
Not only have they come off a test tour of Zimbabwe, they've also won their two first-class tour matches in New Zealand.
They beat a strong Selection 11 by an innings and 113 runs in Palmerston North, then trounced Northern Districts by 10 wickets at Hamilton, both wins achieved effectively inside three days.
By contrast, New Zealand's top players haven't had a first-class game since returning from Pakistan in early December, apart from those who were in the Selection 11.
They have had to rely on a surfeit of Shell Cup one-day matches, plus this week's two-day practice game against an Auckland 11, to get themselves ready for a competitive test rubber.
"I think it's quite a big handicap," Germon told NZPA last night.
"But it's out of our hands, we can't really control it much.
"In some ways it's mental preparation we're going to have to rely on.
"We can't prepare as well as we would have liked to and that means we're going to have to be mentally right-on for the test match."
Germon believes today and tomorrow are crucial for the New Zealand 12, considering the buildup they have -- or haven't -- had for the first test.
"Now we've got two days to sharpen up, put a bit of extra pace into what we're doing."
Germon has been delighted at the spirit within the squad.

Nine of the 12 completed the tour of Pakistan, the odd ones out being fast bowler Danny Morrison, who had to return early because of injury, left arm spinner Mark Haslam, who was named for the tour, then got injured and missed out, and recalled opener Blair Pocock.
"The team has come together really well again," Germon added.
"They are positive and have worked pretty hard."
